title: Permea Evaluation Protocol
description: How the evaluation is run. Encodes the Condition A vs B design as a protocol REQUIREMENT rather than a courtesy: both conditions are always run, and the identity-controlled condition is always the headline.

conditions.$comment: BOTH conditions are always run and always reported. Reporting only the identity-controlled number hides how much leakage the field's prior numbers contained; reporting only the uncontrolled number is the original sin. The DELTA is the finding.

headline_condition.$comment: Schema-constrained to B. This single line is the contract's sharpest edge: an uncontrolled number may be reported, but it may never be THE number.

required_baselines.$comment: A run without these is INVALID, not merely weak. composition_only is the load-bearing one: if a model does not beat 20-dim amino-acid composition under Condition B, it has demonstrated no sequence-specific signal, and any claim built on it is unsupported. length_only is the cheapest and most brutal control there is.

models.description: Models under evaluation, beyond the required baselines.

representations.description: Feature representations. Registry-resolved; free-form so third-party representations are first-class.

fixed_across_conditions.$comment: MUST be true. Re-tuning the threshold separately in A and B makes the A-vs-B delta uninterpretable: you would be measuring threshold movement, not generalisation loss. This is a subtle and very common error.

resample_unit.$comment: DEFAULT cluster. Under identity control the independent unit IS the cluster, not the row -- rows within a cluster are near-duplicates and carry no independent information. Row-level resampling therefore understates the CI, sometimes badly. Choosing 'row' emits PERMEA-W003.

paired.description: A and B deltas are computed on the SAME bootstrap resample indices. Unpaired comparison discards the correlation between conditions and inflates the interval.

family.$comment: The test family must be ENUMERATED UP FRONT, before results are seen. This is a pre-registration hook, and it is the difference between a correction and a rationalisation. 'declared' means the family is listed in family_members.

family_members.description: Test identifiers, declared before the run. e.g. ['B_minus_A:pr_auc:rf:esm2_150m', ...]

allOf.$comment: Bootstrap with n_boot=0 is not inference.

negative_controls.$comment: These must PASS or the run is marked suspect: they verify the harness itself is not manufacturing signal. A pipeline that reports above-chance performance on permuted labels is broken, and no amount of downstream rigour rescues it.

minimum_reporting.$comment: A conformant report MUST contain all of these. This is what stops a conformant-but-selective report: you cannot claim the badge and then publish only the flattering half.

split_policy_ref.description: 'random' = uncontrolled splits; 'primary' = the benchmark's declared split_policy.

report_as.description: An uncontrolled condition may only ever be reported as an optimistic upper bound.

allOf.$comment: Condition A can never be the headline. Enforced structurally, not by convention.
